verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'When 2027'; R3: 'launched by mid-2027 as a low-Earth orbit'; R5: Artemis III mission described with launch details (NASA sites).
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources (R1, R5) confirm 2027 target; R3 explicitly states 'mid-2027' per NASA announcement.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test... rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft'; R5: 'test integrated operations... rendezvous and docking capabilities... Artemis III crew'.
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches NASA descriptions of crewed LEO docking test with commercial landers.

verifications.claim: Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch crew in the Orion spacecraft on top of the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R5: 'Artemis III crew will launch in Orion on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'.
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources directly confirm SLS and Orion for Artemis III crew launch.

verifications.claim: Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test... with one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'; R4: 'SpaceX Starship lunar lander... for Artemis 3'; R5: 'one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin... test rendezvous and docking'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm docking with SpaceX (Starship HLS) lander in LEO.

verifications.claim: Artemis III mission involves docking in low-Earth orbit rather than immediately landing on the Moon, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'low Earth orbit... test rendezvous and docking... needed to land astronauts on the Moon'; R3: 'low-Earth orbit designed to test essential technologies' (no landing); R5: 'low Earth orbit will test... docking capabilities... needed to land astronauts on the Moon'.
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe LEO docking test, not lunar landing for Artemis III.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the Artemis III revision follows concerns over technological readiness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (Guardian): 'technical glitches... too risky... aerospace safety advisory panel... rethink... demanding mission goals'; R4 (SpaceNews): 'potential delays in hardware... Starship... problems SpaceX has had'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact sources cited discuss revisions due to tech delays and safety concerns.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: LEO test of 'commercial landers... needed to land astronauts'; R4: 'delays in... Starship vehicle, including the lunar lander version... for Artemis 3'; R5: 'test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin (HLS)'.
verifications.reasoning: Revision to LEO HLS docking test directly addresses HLS (Starship) delays highlighted in sources.

verifications.claim: The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Guardian directly states landing shifted from III to IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV mission is now targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'.
